title: Historical Data Backfill Costs for Social Listening in 2026
summary: Only one social listening vendor publishes real backfill pricing in 2026. See what 6-24 months of historical data costs — and why most vendors won't say.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Most social listening vendors treat backfill pricing the way they treat enterprise pricing generally: undisclosed. Of nine major platforms compared for 2026 — Awario, Determ, Brand24, YouScan, Mention, Brandwatch, Meltwater, Sprout Social, and Talkwalker — only Syncly publishes an exact per-month and bundled rate for extending historical data ($600/month all-platform, $500/month video-only). Meltwater and Sprout Social confirm that 12- and 24-month backfill options exist, but neither publishes what they cost, and getting a real number requires a sales conversation everywhere except Syncly.


Here's the uncomfortable part: you can't actually shop for backfill. You can shop for a social listening platform, sign a contract, then discover mid-onboarding what it costs to see data from before you signed up. That's not a footnote. For any brand validating a seasonal pattern, investigating a past spike, or building a pre-launch baseline, backfill pricing is a real line item most vendors keep off their pricing pages entirely.


This piece breaks down what backfill actually is, what it costs where costs are disclosed, and — just as important — where they aren't, so you know what to ask before you get on a sales call.


## What is backfill in social listening, and why isn't it included by default?


**Backfill** : the ability to pull historical mentions — posts and conversations that existed before you started tracking a topic — into a social listening query, rather than only collecting data going forward from setup day. A query with 30 days of backfill can tell you what's happening right now; a query with 12+ months can tell you whether that's a spike or a pattern.


Backfill isn't included by default for a simple reason: most[social listening platforms](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) aren't continuously indexing the entire social web in the background. They activate collection the moment you create a topic or query, and pulling older data means a separate, resource-intensive retrieval job against each platform's API — one that's often rate-limited or restricted by the network itself. That's why even "free" backfill windows tend to be short and platform-dependent rather than a flat number.


It also explains why backfill defaults cluster so tightly at the low end. Brand24, YouScan, and Sprout Social all auto-collect roughly the last 30 days when you create a new topic (Source:[Brand24 Help](https://help.brand24.com/en/articles/5336549-does-brand24-collect-historical-data) ;[YouScan Help](https://help.youscan.io/en/articles/461541-how-to-collect-historical-data) ;[Sprout Social Support](https://support.sproutsocial.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056024132-Social-Listening-data-availability-and-limitations) ). Determ is a modest step up at 3 months on every plan (Source:[Determ Pricing FAQ](https://determ.com/pricing/) ). Syncly's default is 1 month free per query — leaner than Determ, but paired with the one thing none of the 30-day vendors offer: a published price for extending it (Source: Syncly pricing, 2026).


## How much does 6 months of backfill cost compared to 12 and 24 months?


Here's the honest answer: a clean 6/12/24-month dollar comparison only exists for one vendor.[Syncly](https://syncly.app/social) is the sole platform in this research with fully public per-month and bundled backfill pricing — every other vendor either includes a short free window with no disclosed paid extension, or confirms a paid option exists and simply won't say what it costs.


Syncly's rate card (Source: Syncly pricing, 2026):


-


**All-platform backfill** : $600 for each additional month, $1,620 for a 3-month package (10% off), $2,880 for a 6-month package (20% off)


-


**Video-only backfill** : $500 for each additional month, $1,350 for a 3-month package, $2,400 for a 6-month package


-


**Maximum lookback** : capped at 1 year


Using that rate card, 6 months of all-platform backfill (on top of the 1 month free) runs $2,880, and since Syncly caps at a 1-year maximum, "24 months" isn't a purchasable option there at all — it's a ceiling, not a missing tier. That cap is worth noting on its own: Syncly trades a hard 1-year limit for being the only vendor that will actually tell you the price before you ask.


For the other eight vendors, the honest number for "12 months" or "24 months" of backfill is: unknown until you talk to sales. Meltwater and Sprout Social are the two vendors that explicitly confirm 12- and 24-month backfill exists as a purchasable option — Sprout Social names both tiers directly — but neither publishes a rate (Source:[Sprout Social Support](https://support.sproutsocial.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056024132-Social-Listening-data-availability-and-limitations) ). A third-party analysis (not confirmed by Meltwater itself) estimates a 24- to 36-month extension might add 10-20% to a base contract — useful context, but an unverified estimate, not a quoted price (Source:[Merciv](https://www.merciv.com/blog/meltwater-pricing-enterprise-teams) ).


That gap is the actual finding here, not a limitation of this research.


## Which social listening vendors charge for backfill, and which include it free?


Short answer: nobody charges nothing, and almost nobody publishes what "charge" means in dollars. What varies is the size of the free window and whether a paid extension is even documented. A few things stand out. Awario's "free" backfill is really a set of API restrictions — Twitter/X is stuck at 7 days regardless of plan, because that's the platform's own limit, not Awario's choice (Source:[Awario blog](https://awario.com/blog/twitter-hashtag-analytics/) ). Mention is the starkest case of paywalling: there's no free historical data at all, and the add-on only exists on its $599/month annual Company Plan — with the price of the add-on itself still undisclosed (Source:[Mention Help](https://en.support.mention.com/en/articles/4052586-activate-historical-data-in-your-alert) ). And Sprout Social is the only vendor here that flatly rules out backfilling a specific major platform — Instagram — at any price, which matters a lot if your brand lives on Instagram.


## How far back can social listening tools actually pull historical data?


It depends far more on vendor philosophy than on technical capability. Some platforms cap lookback hard regardless of budget; others market multi-year archives gated behind a custom quote rather than a fixed limit.


Syncly sits at the conservative end on purpose, with a flat 1-year ceiling regardless of how much backfill you buy (Source: Syncly pricing, 2026). Meltwater's Explore product caps at 15 months — and unusually, Meltwater's own staff have confirmed in their community forum that this limit comes from the underlying source APIs, not a pricing decision, with a newer "Explore+" product teased as the fix but not priced publicly (Source:[Meltwater Community](https://community.meltwater.com/new-to-meltwater-125/historical-data-going-back-farther-than-15-months-3307) ). At the other end, Brandwatch and Talkwalker both market multi-year archives — Brandwatch back to 2008-2010, Talkwalker "up to 5 years" — but both require a custom enterprise quote to actually access that depth (Source:[Brandwatch](https://www.brandwatch.com/blog/introducing-unlimited-historical-data-instant-historical-insight/) ;[Talkwalker](https://www.talkwalker.com/social-intelligence-product) ).


The practical takeaway: a vendor's marketed maximum lookback and what you can actually afford to unlock are two different numbers, and only one shows up on the pricing page. For more on balancing lookback depth with day-to-day monitoring, see our guide to[real-time and historical social listening](https://syncly.app/blog/real-time-and-historical-social-listening) .


## How should a brand decide how many months of backfill to buy?


Start with what the data is actually for. Brands generally need 2-3 years of clean historical listening data to reliably tell a genuine seasonal pattern apart from a one-off spike (Source:[Social Media Markets](https://socialmedia.markets/how-seasonal-trends-affect-social-media-listening-data/) ). That's a considerably higher bar than any vendor's free default — the 30-day-to-3-month range most platforms offer out of the box falls well short of it.


In practice, real backfill needs tend to sort into three buckets:


1.


**Launch or campaign context (1-3 months)** — understanding the conversation immediately before a product launch, rebrand, or crisis. The free defaults at Brand24, YouScan, and Sprout Social (and Syncly's 1 month) roughly cover this.


2.


**Trend and competitive baselining (6-12 months)** — establishing what "normal" volume and sentiment look like across a full sales cycle or a year of seasonality. This is where Syncly's priced tiers ($2,880 for 6 months all-platform) become relevant, and where Meltwater's or Sprout Social's undisclosed 12-month options would need a sales call to price out.


3.


**True seasonality and historical research (24-36 months)** — the range that actual research on seasonal patterns points to as necessary. Most vendors, including Syncly's 1-year cap, don't reach this without a workaround; Brandwatch and Talkwalker's marketed archives are the closest fit, at custom-quote pricing (Source:[Campus Sonar](https://blog.campussonar.com/blog/understanding-the-differences-between-historical-and-ongoing-social-listening) ).


Before you sign anything, ask every vendor on your shortlist three direct questions: what's the default free backfill window, is a paid extension actually available (not just "possible"), and what does it cost per month or as a package. If the answer to the third question is "let's set up a call," treat that as useful information on its own — it tells you the number is negotiable, probably tied to your total contract size, and worth pushing on before you commit. For the full picture of what social listening costs beyond just backfill, see our[social listening pricing benchmarks](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-pricing-benchmarks-2026-what-brands-actually-pay-by-tier) .


## Key Takeaways


-


Only Syncly publishes exact backfill pricing in 2026 — $600/month all-platform or $500/month video-only, with 3- and 6-month package discounts. Every other vendor compared either has no documented paid extension or won't disclose the price.


-


Free default backfill windows cluster tightly around 30 days (Brand24, YouScan, Sprout Social) to 3 months (Determ); Syncly's 1-month default is leaner but paired with transparent extension pricing.


-


Sprout Social is the only vendor that explicitly rules out backfilling a major platform — Instagram — at any price, which matters most for beauty, fashion, and F&B brands.


-


Maximum lookback varies by philosophy, not just budget: Syncly hard-caps at 1 year, Meltwater's Explore caps at 15 months by API limitation, and Brandwatch and Talkwalker market multi-year archives gated behind custom quotes.


-


Brands need roughly 2-3 years of clean historical data to distinguish real seasonality from a one-off spike — well beyond what any vendor's free default provides, which is the practical case for budgeting for backfill at all.


Backfill pricing being opaque isn't an accident of this particular category — it's the same undisclosed-pricing pattern that shows up everywhere in social listening once you look past the entry tier. Until that changes industry-wide, the fastest way to avoid a mid-onboarding surprise is to ask for the backfill number before you ask for the demo.
